title: Secret Sauce curated recipe
description: One authored recipe, in the shape the app's own model uses. Fields map 1:1 onto `recipes` / `ingredient_groups` / `ingredients` / `step_groups` / `steps` in supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql — see docs/SDS.md §3-§6. `tool/recipes.dart` validates against these rules and generates supabase/seed_recipes.sql; it does NOT read this file (no JSON Schema dependency in the toolchain), so a rule added here must be added there too.

slug.description: Repo-level identity. MUST equal the filename without .json — that is what makes duplicates impossible by construction. Not a database column: `recipes` has no slug, and seed_recipe_v2 still dedupes on (owner_id, title), so renaming `title` creates a second row even if the slug is unchanged.

title.description: recipes.title. The de-facto import key — see `slug`.

description.description: recipes.description. Shown truncated on recipe cards, so lead with the dish. Yield that does not fit an integer `servings` (pan size, tart diameter, piece count) belongs here.

cuisine.description: recipes.cuisine. Free text in Postgres; keep it to a recognisable cuisine name so Discover's filters stay coherent.

category.description: recipes.category. Free text in Postgres; this enum is a repo convention only, to stop 'Mains'/'Main'/'main' drift.

difficulty.description: recipes.difficulty — the Postgres `difficulty` enum, mirrored in packages/core/lib/src/models/enums.dart. Wire values are lowercase.

prep_minutes.description: recipes.prep_minutes — hands-on time only. Unattended time (chilling, rising, marinating) goes on the step that waits, as duration_minutes, so the detail screen can show it as a timer instead of inflating the headline time.

servings.description: recipes.servings — an integer because the recipe detail screen scales every ingredient quantity by target/servings. Free text here is what made the old flat data unusable.

visibility.description: recipes.visibility — the Postgres `recipe_visibility` enum. Curated kitchen recipes are public; RLS is what actually enforces this.

attribution.description: recipes.attribution — where the recipe came from, if not original.

notes.description: Recipe-level note (variation, substitution, make-ahead). `recipes` has NO notes column, so tool/recipes.dart appends this to `description` as a trailing paragraph. Lossless but not ideal — a real `notes` column is the proper fix (docs/ROADMAP.md).

nutrition.description: recipes.nutrition — the per-serving nutrition-facts label, as ONE jsonb column rather than eleven numerics. Values are per serving at THIS recipe's `servings` and are never multiplied by the detail screen's servings scaler (scaling 4->8 doubles the batch and the servings, so a serving is unchanged). Every field is optional; `null` — not `{}` — is the one representation of "no nutrition info", and the detail screen's Nutrition tab renders its empty state from it. Mirrored by RecipeNutrition in packages/core and by _nutritionKeys in tool/recipe_format.dart; unknown keys are a hard error there because the jsonb column itself would accept them. `source` is the twelfth key and the only non-numeric one (Phase 29c).

calories.description: kcal per serving. No % Daily Value is printed for calories, as on a real label.

saturated_fat_g.description: Grams, indented under total fat. %DV against 20 g.

trans_fat_g.description: Grams, indented under total fat. No %DV — there is no established daily value.

dietary_fiber_g.description: Grams, indented under total carbohydrate. %DV against 28 g.

total_sugars_g.description: Grams, indented under total carbohydrate. No %DV — only added sugars carry one.

added_sugars_g.description: Grams, indented under total sugars. %DV against 50 g.

source.description: Provenance (Phase 29c). `"auto"` means the eleven numbers above were computed from this file's ingredient `food` links by estimate_nutrition() — the label then prints an `Estimated from ingredients` footnote. MANUAL IS SPELLED BY ABSENCE: there is no `"manual"` value, which is what made the key migration-free for every label written before it existed. An object carrying ONLY `source` is rejected like an empty one — use `null` for "no info". Regenerate an auto label whenever the recipe's ingredients or nutritionData/ change; `recompute_auto_nutrition()` in 0001_init.sql does the same job for a database that already holds the recipe.

ingredient_groups.description: ingredient_groups rows, in array order (sort_order 0..n). Use one group with an empty name for a simple recipe; use named groups whenever the same ingredient appears at two amounts in two components (marinade vs sauce), because a flat list makes that read like a duplicate.

name.description: ingredient_groups.name. Empty string for the single unnamed group.

step_groups.description: step_groups rows, in array order (sort_order 0..n). step_order restarts at 0 in each group, matching SupabaseRecipeRepository._persistContent — numbering continuously across groups would silently renumber every step the first time a user edited the recipe.

name.description: step_groups.name. Empty string for the single unnamed group.

demo.description: DEMO FIXTURES, NOT CONTENT. Fake engagement so a curated recipe ranks plausibly on Discover and the chef leaderboard. Delete this block (and the fixture accounts in supabase/seed.sql) when the demo data is retired — the recipe itself survives without it.

quantity.description: ingredients.quantity (Postgres numeric). Decimal, never a fraction string — '1 1/4 cup' cannot be scaled, 1.25 can. Null for 'to taste' / 'for frying' style entries; put the qualifier in `note`. For a range, use the amount you would actually reach for and describe the range in `note`.

unit.description: ingredients.unit. Null for countable items ('2 eggs'). Keep spelling consistent across files: cup, tsp, Tbsp, oz, lb, g, ml, cloves, pinch, bunch, pkg, pint.

name.description: ingredients.name — the ingredient alone, lowercase unless it is a proper noun (Dijon, Gruyère, Gouda). Preparation goes in `note`, not here.

note.description: ingredients.note — preparation or qualifier ('finely chopped', 'to taste', 'divided').

is_optional.description: ingredients.is_optional. Use this instead of writing '(optional)' into the name.

food.description: ingredients.food_id — the link into the food registry (Phase 29b). Must be a slug that exists in nutritionData/foods.json; tool/recipe_format.dart enforces that, because the generated SQL carries it into a real FK column. Optional and invisible to every rendered surface: `name` stays the cook's words, this is what auto nutrition (29c) sums. Leave it off for the documented registry gaps (mirin, spice blends, composites — see nutritionData/README.md).

text.description: steps.text — one action per step. Every ingredient a step names must exist in ingredient_groups; every ingredient must be used by some step. tool/recipes.dart warns on both (that mismatch was the whole of B025).

duration_minutes.description: steps.duration_minutes — drives the in-step timer. Set it for waits too (chill, rise, marinate); those are deliberately excluded from prep_minutes.

temperature.description: steps.temperature, as written to the cook, e.g. '350°F' or 'medium-low'.

tip.description: steps.tip — the doneness cue or the thing that goes wrong. Rendered as an aside, so it must not carry an instruction the step needs.

ratings.description: One rating per seeded taster account, in pool order (seed_taster_ids() in supabase/seed.sql, 8 accounts — extras are ignored). Half-star steps only; the same 0.5-5.0 check constraint applies as to a real rating.
